newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end tad down in thin volume.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end tad down in thin volume.

text.p: * Composite index down 4.62, or 0.15 pct, at 3,115.58 points
Manila stocks ended slightly down on Monday in thin volume as investors opted to remain on the sidelines due to the Christmas holiday mood and the Dow's lacklustre performance, traders said.

"At this time of this year, with the holidays nearing, people are not that excited in investing in the stock market. So we won't see much activity" said Caesar Tanquingcen, trader at Cornell Securities Inc.
"Market is still lagging, as unfortunately people are still watching the Dow, and it's fall last week still has that psychological carryover," Irving Ackerman at I. Ackerman & Co Inc said.
Value turnover was below average at 1.59 billion pesos.
Losers outweighed gainers at 71 to 36 with 83 issues unchanged. But traders said that decliners shed minimal points.
Most blue chips were down but bucking the trend were San Miguel B and Ayala Land B.

These two shares had faced the brunt of selling last week when the Philippine market along with the U.S. and most Asian markets fell on Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's comment on "irrational exuberance" in the financial markets.
Cilette Liboro, research head at Citisecurities Inc, said the market will continue to await the outcome of the Federal Reserve's meeting on Tuesday.
